findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how path 2 produces uv.lock (e.g. on a fresh worktree run `uv lock --upgrade-package ruff` to bump only ruff while mcp stays `<2`, do NOT apply PR #124's lock), since PR #124's lock embeds mcp 2.0.0 + mcp-types and cannot be reused verbatim under the kept `<2` pin.
evidence: Plan: 'Apply each PR's diff verbatim (gh pr diff N | git apply), never retyped by hand, so the landed content is byte-identical'
Plan path 2: 'the documented safe subset (ruff bump, mcp kept <2, _optionality.yml and ADR 0050 untouched)'

PR #124 per the plan loosens the constraint '>=1.28.1,<2 -> <3' and adds 'new transitive mcp-types package in uv.lock' — a lock that keeping <2 cannot contain, so PR #124's uv.lock is unusable verbatim on path 2
Verified installed mcp resolves FastMCP (v1), consistent with a <2 lock differing structurally from PR #124's <3 lock
findings.finding: Path 2's 'safe subset' mechanism is under-specified and conflicts with the plan's own verbatim-diff invariant: PR #124's uv.lock was generated with mcp 2.0.0 + the new mcp-types transitive + the <3 constraint, so it cannot be `git apply`-ed while keeping mcp <2. The path-2 lock must be REGENERATED, but the plan gives no command or provenance for producing it.
findings.location: Change B, path 2 ('Land the safe subset ... ruff 0.16.1 bump + uv.lock refresh with mcp kept <2')
scenarios: Path 2 triggers (structural mcp v2 breakage); implementer tries to `git apply` PR #124's uv.lock keeping mcp <2 and gets an incoherent or conflicting lock
A hand-edited path-2 lock drifts from what `uv lock` would deterministically produce, breaking reproducibility that other consumers' pre-commit/CI depend on
findings.suggested_fix: In path 2, state that pyproject keeps `mcp ... <2`, ruff is bumped in the dev group, and the lock is regenerated with `uv lock --upgrade-package ruff` (not `gh pr diff 124 | git apply`); note that this is the one place where the verbatim-diff rule is deliberately waived and why.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the Change A byte-fidelity `git diff` pathspec to cover the allowlist echo lines' actual location (or drop the `-- .github/workflows` limiter) so the comparison against `/tmp/pr123.diff` includes every file the PR touches.
evidence: `git diff <base>..HEAD -- .github/workflows | diff - /tmp/pr123.diff`
PR #123 described as '13 workflow files + the allowlist echo lines' and 'updates the two `echo` allowlist lines'
AC1 requires byte-identical to `gh pr diff 123` INCLUDING allowlist echo lines
findings.finding: The Change A byte-fidelity verification command scopes the diff to `.github/workflows` but compares it against the full PR #123 diff, which also includes the two allowlist echo lines — if those echo lines live outside `.github/workflows`, the diff will spuriously mismatch.
scenarios: The allowlist echo lines reside in a file not under .github/workflows, causing the pathspec-limited left side to omit lines present on the right side and the diff to report differences even on a faithful apply.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm where the allowlist echo lines live; if inside the workflow files the current command is fine, otherwise use `git diff <base>..HEAD | diff - /tmp/pr123.diff` (unscoped) to match the full PR diff.

findings.finding: The plan treats a capability question that documented, current prior art already resolves as an open test outcome, and picks the wrong branch as 'expected.' It says 'Whether 2.0 keeps these paths as compat shims is exactly what the test suite must decide' and designates path 1 (compat shims hold) as the '(expected path).' But the upstream migration guide the plan itself references states FastMCP is renamed to MCPServer with the old mcp.server.fastmcp import path removed (not shimmed), and mcp.types moved to a separate mcp-types package with the old import path removed. At least two of the five named v1 import sites (src/rebar/mcp_server.py:570 mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP; src/rebar/_mcp_models.py:287 mcp.types.ToolAnnotations) are therefore known-broken under 2.0 before any test runs. The appearance of a new mcp-types transitive package in uv.lock — which the plan notes — is itself confirmation the types path moved.
findings.location: Problem section ('The mcp major is the risk...' paragraph) and Change B path 1 ('Compat shims hold (expected path)')
scenarios: Author executes path 1 as the default, spends a full make test/lint/typecheck cycle re-discovering a rename upstream already documents, then has to unwind to path 2.

Path-1 'mechanical 1:1 import-path renames' balloon into real migration (module rename + mcp.types->mcp-types package split), colliding with the plan's own OUT-of-scope 'non-mechanical mcp v2 migration work' clause.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Problem section, replace 'whether 2.0 keeps these paths as compat shims is exactly what the test suite must decide' with a resolved statement grounded in the migration guide (FastMCP->MCPServer, module path gone; mcp.types->mcp-types, path removed), and in Change B mark path 2 as the expected path. Keep path 1 only as the fallback if the test suite unexpectedly passes.
